inputs.share_count_basis: Shares outstanding at 30 June 2026: subscribed capital EUR 529,095,195 / EUR 3.00 nominal = 176.37m issued, less 563,156 treasury shares (3rd buyback tranche) = 175.80m (H1-2026 report, treasury-share note). Basic = diluted (no material dilutive instruments; EPS reported 'basic and diluted'). Held FLAT: SBC is immaterial (SBC-zero market) and continuing buybacks are cash returns funded from the flows/net debt, value-neutral in this model. The parser's FY2025 177.7m is a weighted average and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR: LTIP capital-market component expense EUR 1-2m/yr (immaterial, cash-settled components already inside personnel costs/RCOBD); no equity-award taxes. Treated as an SBC-zero market; SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:30Z (Xetra closing auction, Friday regular close; valuation run on Sunday 2026-10-25)
inputs.last_fcf_basis: UNLEVERED owner FCF FY2025, as the engine projects it: OCF 3,254.8 + interest paid 356.2 - interest received 160.5 = 3,450.5 pre-financing OCF; less net capex 1,195.3 (PP&E 1,364.6 + intangibles 50.0 - grants 73.6 - PP&E disposals 145.7); less lease renewal 249 (right-of-use depreciation, lease treatment A) = ~2,006 (9.3% of revenue). reported_fcf 1,840.2 is the parser's levered OCF - gross capex. FY2024 on the same basis ~2,012.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.2 (cyclical, carbon-intensive) -> cost of equity ~9.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.75% (2026 EUR bond coupon), ~2.8% after tax. Market weights: equity ~EUR 26.0bn (175.8m x price), debt-like ~EUR 8.3bn (net debt incl. leases + pensions) -> ~23% debt. WACC ~7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality is charged in the bear-weighted scenario flows, not as a rate premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (~EUR 1.19bn at Dec-2025) sit inside the company's net debt and inside total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged through capex_pct_path (+~1.1pp of revenue, = FY2025 right-of-use depreciation EUR 249m). RCOBD is post-IFRS-16, so no lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at market-proxy value EUR 2,000m (~10.6x FY2025 NCI profit of EUR 188.6m; ~1.7x NCI book of EUR 1,170m at 30-Jun-2026). Akcansa (consolidated from 18-Jun-2026, 20.56% NCI) is inside the June NCI book. NCI put options (EUR 56m) are already inside company net debt.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined net debt EUR 7,726m at 30 June 2026 (H1-2026 key figures; bonds + bank loans + other financial liabilities incl. leases and NCI puts, less cash and current interest-bearing receivables). June is the seasonal working-capital peak; the H1-2026 unlevered FCF deficit (~EUR -434m: OCF 35.6 + interest paid 202.7 - interest received 86.2 - net capex 461.2 - leases ~125) is also contained in the FY2026 year-1 flow, so it is added back in the equity bridge to avoid charging it twice. H1-2026 acquisitions (Akcansa majority, others; EUR 588m) are inside the June net debt and their revenue is inside the FY2026-27 growth path.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Heidelberg Materials is an integrated cement/aggregates/ready-mix manufacturer: an operating company whose value is unlevered free cash flow -- not a bank, REIT, LIC or holdco. First valuation (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). EBITDA_MARGIN_PATH IS CASH-CONVERTED RCOBD: reported RCOBD (21.8% FY2025) less ~2.0pp of recurring cash leakage that sits between RCOBD and OCF (provision utilisation EUR 256m, non-cash equity-accounted result in excess of dividends received, restructuring cash in the additional ordinary result, discontinued ops). Calibrated so FY2025 actuals reproduce the EUR 2,006m unlevered owner FCF: cash EBITDA 4,255 (19.8%) - D&A 1,298 = EBIT 2,957; cash tax 716 = 24.2% of that EBIT. MID-CYCLE: FY2025 RCOBD margin 21.8% is the series high (2019-2025 range 17.7-21.8%, avg 20.2%); the base case fades toward ~20.8% RCOBD (18.8% cash) rather than capitalising the peak. Excluded base years: FY2020 (EUR 3.1bn COVID-era impairments, WC release flattered FCF to 2,057) and FY2021 (cash tax 25.8%, EUR 747m one-off). PENDING/EXCLUDED: the Maas Group construction-materials acquisition (Australia, preliminary price ~EUR 1bn; completion H2-2026, not in the 30-Jun balance sheet) is left out of BOTH the flows and net debt -- value-neutral at a fair price; a reader adding it should add ~EUR 1bn of net debt and its revenue together. Buybacks: a repurchaser (EUR 400m FY2025, EUR 102m H1-2026 of the final EUR 400m tranche); the flat count is being funded. Analysis JSON (HEI.DE_Analysis.json, 2026-10-25) was available and its bull/bear axes drive the scenarios.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: cycle-adjusted: base-case 10-year revenue path averages ~3.0%, between the 3yr revenue CAGR (0.6%, a flat-volume European downturn) and the 5yr (4.0%, inflation pass-through pricing plus M&A). Equity 5yr CAGR (6.5%) is inflated by the FY2020 impairment trough base and is not used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.5% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 4.0% (+62% divergence): the FY2020 base sits after EUR 3.1bn of impairments, so book growth overstates underlying compounding. EPS 5yr CAGR undefined (FY2020 EPS -10.78).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF here (SBC ~0, equity-award taxes 0, interest income not stripped because the company carries net DEBT). FCF 3yr CAGR of 19.3% starts from the FY2022 energy-shock trough (1,085) and 5yr -2.2% from the FY2020 COVID working-capital release (2,057); neither is a usable trend. FCF has been flat at ~EUR 1.82-1.88bn levered for FY2023-25.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +4.5%: H1 +1.7% reported (+2.8% LfL, FX drag), H2 adds Akcansa consolidation (~1.5pp of group) and prior bolt-ons; FY2027 +4.0% carries the Akcansa annualisation; then 2.5-3% nominal (EUR/USD inflation pricing, flat-to-low volumes), 2% terminal. Maas excluded.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Cash RCOBD. FY2026 19.5% ~ RCOBD 21.5% (guidance RCO 3.40-3.65bn midpoint on ~22.4bn revenue, H1 margin -59bps); fades to 18.8% (~20.8% RCOBD) as the 2023-25 pricing cycle normalises toward the 2019-25 average with some credit for the NA/aggregates mix shift.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guidance net PP&E 1.2-1.3bn + intangibles ~50 + lease renewal ~250 = ~6.9% of revenue; Strategy-2030 average ~1.3bn net plus CCS (Padeswood, Airvault) keeps it elevated to FY2028; terminal 6.6% vs D&A 6.0% funds 2% growth.
base.tax_note: Cash tax on EBIT 24.2% in FY2025 (716 / 2,957); 24.5% held. FY2021 25.8% was an abnormal one-off year.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: inventories + receivables - payables ~8.5% of revenue, so growth consumes cash (negative capture).
base.narrative: Mid-cycle base: European construction stabilises (Euroconstruct +2% 2026) but residential stays weak; US infrastructure and data-centre demand offset softer housing; prices keep pace with inflation and carbon cost but the 2023-25 margin peak partly normalises. EU ETS free-allocation phase-out (extended to 2038) is broadly passed through behind CBAM.

bull.narrative: Strategy 2030 delivers: RCO compounds ~7% (bottom of the +7-10% target) on a European construction recovery from 2027, US infrastructure/IIJA and data-centre pull, and Australian/Turkish growth; evoZero/CCS turns rising ETS prices into a premium-priced moat (sustainable products 37% of revenue -> majority), lifting RCOBD margin to ~22.7% (cash 20.7%) and ROIC to ~12%.

bear.narrative: Cyclical downturn plus carbon squeeze: rates stay high, European and US residential/commercial volumes fall in 2027-28 (the FY2022 energy-shock margin of 17.7% RCOBD is the template), and post-2030 ETS reform raises net carbon cost faster than CBAM-protected pricing recovers it; integration of Akcansa/Maas dilutes margins. RCOBD settles ~19.5% (cash 17.5%), volumes recover only with inflation.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle: guidance-midpoint FY2026 (RCO ~3.5bn), then the 2023-25 peak pricing margin fades ~1pp as European construction stabilises without a residential recovery and US infrastructure offsets housing; carbon cost broadly passed through behind CBAM; capex held at the Strategy-2030 ~1.3bn plus CCS; 2% terminal growth, 14x terminal FCF cap (cyclical).
scenario_narratives.bull: Strategy 2030 on track: RCO +7% p.a., European recovery from 2027, US infrastructure/data-centre demand, Akcansa/Maas growth geographies, and evoZero/CCS converting rising EU ETS prices into premium pricing and share gains; RCOBD margin to ~22.7%, ROIC ~12%; 16x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2027-28 construction downturn in Europe and North America on persistent high rates, energy-cost spikes (Middle East) and post-2030 ETS reform outpacing pass-through; leverage already 1.66x after the M&A wave limits buybacks; RCOBD margin troughs near FY2022's 17.7% and settles ~19.5%; 12x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): highly cyclical demand, FY2026 guidance already trimmed, H1 OCF -69%, leverage 1.66x above the 1.5x target, and an unresolved post-2030 ETS reform. Base 50%: guidance-consistent mid-cycle path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a European recovery, CCS premium pricing and clean multi-deal integration to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the company on mid-cycle unlevered owner FCF, not on the 2023-25 peak-margin cash flows: cement is a local-oligopoly but cyclical, carbon-intensive business whose margin has ranged 17.7-21.8% RCOBD in seven years. SBC is immaterial, so house and street coincide. Leases are treated as debt (inside company net debt) with lease renewal charged in capex; NCI and pensions are deducted once in the bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is cap-bound (14x terminal FCF ~ 7x EV/RCOBD); a peer re-rating toward CRH/Holcim multiples is upside the model does not grant
EU ETS free-allocation phase-out and post-2030 reform: net carbon cost could exceed pass-through
Construction-cycle volume sensitivity in Europe and North America; FY2026 guidance already lowered
Maas Group acquisition (~EUR 1bn) excluded from both flows and net debt; overpaying would destroy value the model treats as neutral
NCI valued at a market-proxy multiple (EUR 2.0bn) rather than observed prices
